theorem_title: Bounded-degree MAX-CUT and MAX-E2LIN(2): the three-occurrence lift exceeds the Unique Games thresholds ($0.9932>83/84$)
natural_language_statement:
The Unique Games Conjecture limits the approximability of $\mathrm{MAX\text{-}2SAT}$ to $\beta^\star\approx 0.94016567$ and of weighted $\mathrm{MAX\text{-}}\{1,2\}\text{-}\mathrm{HORN\text{-}SAT}$ to $\alpha^*\approx 0.94615981$ on general instances. This theorem shows that a graph $G$ of maximum degree $d$ (a $\mathrm{MAX\text{-}CUT}$ or $\mathrm{MAX\text{-}E2LIN}(2)$ instance) can be encoded as a three-occurrence formula $T_{H(G)}$ whose optimum is approximated within a factor above $0.9932>\tfrac{83}{84}$, which exceeds both thresholds.

The formalized statement says:

- The thresholds are ordered: $0.94016567<0.94615981<\tfrac{83}{84}<0.9932$.
- For a graph $G$ with $m$ edges, every vertex set $S$ selects an independent set of the conflict graph $H(G)$ of size $m+\mathrm{cut}(S)$, and the independence number of $H(G)$ is $m+\mathrm{maxcut}(G)$.
- If $G$ has maximum degree at most $d$, then $H(G)$ has maximum degree at most $d+1$, and the degrees of $H(G)$ add up to $4m+2\sum_v\deg(v)^2$, so $H(G)$ has at least $4m$ edges.
- An independent set of size $s$ with $18785\,\alpha\le 20000\,s$ lifts to an assignment satisfying at least $0.9932$ (hence at least $\tfrac{83}{84}$) of the optimum of the formula.
- For the formula $T_H$ of any port-labelled graph with vertex degrees $d_v$, the optimum is $\sum_v(d_v+1)+m+\alpha$, and the lift of an independent set $I$ satisfies $\sum_v(d_v+1)+m+|I|$ clauses.

The Goemans--Williamson cut guarantee, the running times, the Unique Games hardness thresholds, and the identification of $T_{H(G)}$ with a port-labelled graph are not formalized.
explanation: The threshold comparison is `PaperArithmetic.ugc_thresholds` and `norm_num`. Item (1) is `ConflictGraph.selSet_independent`, `card_selSet`, `CutTransfer.value_eq_edges_add_cut` and `ConflictGraph.alpha_eq`. Item (2) is `ConflictDegree.card_nbrs`. Item (3) sums `card_nbrs` over the occurrences of each variable (`occurrences_eq`, `card_occ`) and uses $d^2\ge d$. Item (4) is linear arithmetic (`omega`). Item (5) is `GeneralDegreeFormula`: the port bijection gives $\sum_v d_v=2m$; the satisfied clauses split as $U(z)+(m-F(z))+(\sum_v(d_v+1)-T(z))$ (`satCount_eq_score`); the cycle lemma and the deletion of one endpoint of every edge between clean vertices give $\mathrm{score}\le\sum_v(d_v+1)+m+|R(z)|$ with $R(z)$ independent (`score_le`); the lift of an independent set attains $\sum_v(d_v+1)+m+|I|$. This submission is supported by a Lean 4 formalization, available at https://github.com/frankvegadelgado/paloma. The formalization covers the exact optimum identities, the repair and lifting steps, and the arithmetic of the approximation ratios. The Goemans–Williamson, Berman–Fujito and Trevisan guarantees are taken from the literature and are stated as explicit hypotheses; the Unique Games thresholds are cited in the paper and are not formalized.
definition_title: Formula $T_H$ for per-vertex degrees, edge-list graphs and the conflict graph of $F_G$
definition_nl: Formal model of the three-occurrence Horn formula $T_H$ of a graph with a port labelling and a degree $d_v$ at every vertex (`GPortGraph`), with $d_v+1$ clones per vertex, its independent sets and independence number, and the number of satisfied clauses (`satCount`); together with graphs given by an edge list (`EdgeGraph`), the cut value (`cutCount`), the literal occurrences of the MAX 2-SAT formula $F_G$ (`Occ`), the conflict graph on them (`Adj`, `Ind`, `nbrs`, `occ`), maximum cut and independence number of the conflict graph (`IsMaxCut`, `IsIndNumber`) and the independent set `selSet` selected by a vertex set.
